ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg law: (i) amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, Title I, Articles 101-107, as inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013, governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); (ii) Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Act), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020, imposing UBO filing for registered entities including SCSp; (iii) amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 9 January 2020 implementing EU Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); (iv) Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 December 2004 on customer identification and verification; and (v) CSSF Circulars 18/681 and 19/732 on AML/CFT and CDD obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national identity card of each individual general partner and each beneficial owner holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil registry, national identity authority or accredited service provider in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention certificate issued by the competent authority in the country of issuance, or consular legalization by the Luxembourg embassy/consulate in the country of issue if the Hague Convention does not apply

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing, corporate extract or register certificate of the corporate general partner (where a corporate entity is used)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry, tribunal de commerce or competent corporate register in the corporate partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate or consular legalization in the issuing state, followed by sworn French translation for submission to the RCS

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of residence or official tax domicile proof for each general partner and each 25%+ beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax administration or residency authority of the country of tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate or consular legalization, with sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for the Luxembourg incorporation counsel or domiciliation agent to sign and file pre-incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or public authority in the jurisdiction where the grantor is located
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate or consular legalization; for online execution, certified qualified electronic signature acceptable in Luxembourg practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and professional/KYC background letter for the general partner and ultimate beneficial owner, confirming source of funds in the Amazon marketplace activity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or relationship bank of the beneficial owner or general partner, or a regulated AML/KYC professional
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the issuing bank is located outside the EU/EEA

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual screening of every general partner and each beneficial owner with a 25% or greater economic interest against: (1) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (EU CFSP lists); (2) United Nations Security Council consolidated security and sanctions lists; (3) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list; (4) Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) consolidated list where relevant; (5) World Bank/EBRD debarment lists; and (6) the national Luxembourg Pruvent list maintained by the CSSF and the Ministry of Finance. Any politically exposed person (PEP) status must be confirmed by electronic screening, documented, documented with enhanced due diligence, and measures must include source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification. Beneficial owners who are PEPs require senior management approval before any transaction is completed. Screening records, risk assessments and CDD files must be retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship pursuant to Article 13 of the amended Luxembourg Anti-Money-Laundering Law. Amazon Pay, Stripe and Airwallex each apply their own KYB/PSD2 verification and may re-screen the SCSp entity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — official online portal: https://www.lbr.lu (RCS name clearance module and electronic filing via eLBR/pLBR; publication in the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All RCS registration documentation must be filed in French or, where expressly accepted, in German or Luxembourgish. The company name itself must be expressed in Latin script; names in non-Latin characters such as Chinese, Cyrillic, Hebrew or Arabic are not admissible unless transliterated into Latin characters in the partnership agreement and accompanied by a sworn transliteration/translation into French. Accents and diacritics using Latin script are permitted. The name must not be contrary to Luxembourg public policy and must not mislead the public as to the legal form, object or regulated status of the SCSp.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS/LBR rejects the requested name, the applicant may immediately submit a new name clearance request with an amended name. To contest a rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative reconsideration request with the RCS within 15 business days of the rejection notice, attaching a copy of the requested name, the refusal grounds, an evidence package showing that the name is distinguishable from existing Luxembourg registered names, and, if necessary, trademark consent letters. If the administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Tribunal d'Ardissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber, within 1 month of the denial. A favorable declaratory judgment then allows a further 30-day name reservation. Any change of legal name after registration requires a formal amendment of the SCSp partnership agreement and re-filing with the RCS.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual postal-only office is not acceptable for an RCS-registered SCSp engaged in cross-border e-commerce. Luxembourg law requires that each registered entity have an actual registered office located at a physical address in Luxembourg where legal correspondence, books and registers are available. However, professional domiciliation agents legally established in Luxembourg and subject to AML supervision may provide a physical registered office address together with mail-handling and physical reception services. Such a domiciliation arrangement is accepted only when the domiciliation agent actually operates at that address and when the SCSp's partners, tax representative and diligence officers are contactable there. A pure virtual address without physical staff or document-keeping capability is not permissible and will not satisfy the RCS or CSSF commercial substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a low-risk internet-retail SCSp using Amazon FBA and standard third-party payment rails, the annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection is estimated at 2-5%. The risk materially increases above 20% if the RBE UBO filing is inconsistent with the notarial or partnership records, if late filing penalties have been imposed, if the SCSp accepts unusual payment methods or third-party funding, or if the RCS receives a request from a bank or payment service provider (Amazon Pay, Stripe, Airwallex) relating to KYB remediation. Luxembourg RCS and CSSF AML authorities are entitled to perform physical on-site inspections at the registered office without prior notice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official name clearance and RCS availability check for the proposed SCSp name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative tariff: estimated EUR 25 plus optional electronic filing surcharge; subject to RCS fee schedule applicable at filing date

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SCSp partnership agreement (acte de société) and contribution provisions by a Luxembourg corporate law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate lawyer / law firm engaged as pre-incorporation counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark for a standard SCSp with one general partner and one limited partner: EUR 2,500-4,000, excluding notarial fees and VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille/consular legalization of foreign identity, corporate standing, tax residence and power-of-attorney documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Luxembourg notary and foreign ministry, embassy or consular authority in the country of issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official notarial fee schedule plus issuing-state apostille/consular tariff; applicable where documents originate outside the EU/EEA or outside the Hague Convention area

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of the SCSp partnership agreement, name clearance certificate and RBE beneficial-owner declarations into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg sworn translator (traducteur agréé) entered in the official list
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page sworn translator tariff: approximately EUR 55-70 per page, estimated for 12-15 certified pages, plus French revision of the legal structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing fee and publication in the electronic companies bulletin (Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS and Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff: EUR 19 for RCS submission plus EUR 15 electronic bulletin publication; amounts reflect Luxembourg official fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial Owner Register (RBE) declaration filing for the SCSp and each UBO
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RBE registration tariff of EUR 0-25 plus professional handling costs; fees are fixed per filing in the RBE online portal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and national sanctions screening and AML customer-due-diligence pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/CFT compliance service provider or Luxembourg domiciliation agent acting under the CSSF regulatory framework
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee for a low-risk standard retail e-commerce SCSp, including WorldCheck/AML automated screening and manual verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service for one calendar quarter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fee: EUR 750-1,200 per quarter for a physical Luxembourg office address, correspondence handling and registry/regulatory notification service

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Articles 94-101 (S.C.S. / S.C.Sp.) and applicable provisions of the Law of 15 February 2021 (amending the 1915 Law); RCS registration under Articles 9-27 of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS) operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized or privately executed partnership agreement (contrat de société) with registration in the RCS via the e-RCS electronic filing portal; publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations - RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SCSp: no minimum share capital or paid-up capital requirement under Luxembourg law; contributions in cash or in kind are governed solely by the partnership agreement; no escrow account obligation unless stipulated in the partnership agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator(s) adopt the partnership agreement of Luxembourg Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) and approve the subscription of all partnership interests as set out therein. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address indicated in the agreement, and the general partner is authorized to register the SCSp with the Luxembourg RCS and to file required publications. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed as general partner, and [Name] be appointed as manager/director for day-to-day management, with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete all filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Verify Availability with Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS desk / e-RCS online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online request via the LBR e-RCS portal or by email to the RCS availability service, providing up to three proposed names. The requested name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. The name must comply with Luxembourg public order rules and should include the abbreviation SCSp or the words 'société en commandite spéciale'. Upon approval, the name is reserved for a period of 30 days (renewable on request). No notarization is required for the name reservation itself.
required_dossiers: Proposed name list (up to 3 choices)
Identification of the incorporator(s) (passport/ID copies)
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a revised name list within the remaining reservation period; if approval is delayed beyond the SLA, follow up via RCS email and request accelerated processing; if the name is confusingly similar to an existing entity, provide consent from that entity or amend the distinctive element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Partnership Agreement and Organizational Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (if notarized) or the general partner(s) acting under the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société) in a language acceptable to the RCS (typically French, German, or English with certified translation). The document must define the entity name, registered office address, purpose (ISIC 4791 internet retail / e-commerce marketplace FBA), capital contributions of the limited partner(s) (which may be zero), duration, management powers of the general partner, distribution waterfall, and governing law. Execute the agreement by all partners; notarization is optional unless real estate or specific contributions are involved. Prepare signed acceptance of office by the general partner and any manager(s).
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Identification documents of all partners (passport/ID)
Address proof of general partner and registered office
Bank confirmation of capital contribution (if any)
Signed acceptance of office by general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries incomplete language or missing clauses, amend the by-laws and refile; if partner identification is insufficient, provide legalized or apostilled copies; if the registered office landlord refuses occupancy, provide an updated lease and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for RCS Registration and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) via e-RCS electronic filing; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic filing through the e-RCS portal, attaching the executed partnership agreement, the statement of subscription of partnership interests, identification of officers, and the registered office address. The application for registration must be completed and signed by the general partner or authorized representative. The RCS will issue a certificate of registration (extrait / certificat) and assign a RCS trade registration number. The filing is automatically published in the RESA electronic compendium, which must occur within one month of registration. The registered office address must be verified by the LBR through a letter of occupancy or supporting lease evidence.
required_dossiers: RCS registration form (formulaire de création) signed by general partner
Executed partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Statement of contributions / subscription of partnership interests
Notice of registered office and occupancy proof (lease or letter from the domiciliation agent)
Certified identification of general partner, manager(s), and limited partner(s)
Fees paid (currently EUR 0 for electronic filing in most cases, with certain publication costs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (e.g., missing occupancy proof), file a supplementary response within 15 days through e-RCS; if registration is suspended due to AML/KYC doubts, provide enhanced due diligence documentation; if RESA publication is delayed, contact the LBR helpline to expedite and request a publication certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Registration, VAT Credential, and EORI Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes - ACD), Luxembourg VAT Administration (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA - AEDT), and Luxembourg Customs (Administration des douanes et accises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the SCSp is automatically identified for direct tax purposes and will be assigned a Luxembourg national business number (numéro d'identification, NIF). Register separately for VAT using the standard Luxembourg VAT registration form (Formulaire 1) via the e-TVA portal or by mail from Rabat/Croix Rouge desk. Request an EORI number through the Luxembourg Customs website (GIE e-commerce portal) for importing goods under an Amazon FBA cross-border model. Note that the SCSp is fiscally transparent; VAT registration is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed EUR 35,000 per year or for distance sales thresholds.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract / certificate
Partnership agreement
Identification of general partner and manager
VAT registration form (Formulaire 1)
Business activity description (internet retail via marketplace)
EORI application form (if importing goods)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT application is delayed, escalate to the AEDT taxpayer service; if the EORI application is rejected, provide a supporting customs broker power of attorney and resubmit; if the NIF is not generated automatically, apply via ACD form 107.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Corporate Bank Account and Appoint Payment Service Providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks operating in Luxembourg (e.g., BGL BNP Paribas, BCEE, Spuerkeess) or licensed EMI/PSP (e.g., Airwallex, Stripe) with Luxembourg access
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS registration extract, partnership agreement, identification of all beneficial owners (ultimate beneficial owners), proof of registered office, and business plan (Amazon FBA e-commerce). Complete the bank's KYC/AML onboarding and beneficial ownership declaration (register of beneficial owners - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE). Connect payment rails (Amazon Pay, Stripe, Airwallex) as required by the business scope, ensuring the SCSp's legal name and tax identification are used for pay-out accounts. For Airwallex or Stripe, complete additional merchant verification in the name of the SCSp with the general partner's authorization.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate / extract
Partnership agreement
UBO declaration to the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
Passport/ID of general partner and managers
Proof of address of registered office
Business plan / projected revenue
AML questionnaire and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a compliance hold, provide beneficial ownership chart and commercial invoices; if the bank refuses due to the pass-through nature of the SCSp, select an alternative bank or EMI with a specialized e-commerce onboarding; escalate to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) only in cases of discriminatory refusal under applicable rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Beneficial Owner Declaration with the RBE Register and Ensure Ongoing Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration and within one month, submit the declaration of ultimate beneficial owners to the RBE. Identify any natural person owning or controlling more than 25% of the partnership interests or who otherwise exercises control through other means. The declaration must be made by the general partner through the LBR e-RCS portal. The SCSp is required to maintain an internal register mirroring the RBE filing, and any changes must be filed within one month.
required_dossiers: RBE declaration form (electronic)
Evidence of ownership percentages
Identification of each beneficial owner
General partner's authorizing resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE declaration is queried, supplement the documentation demonstrating ownership or control; if penalties are threatened for late filing, file on the same day and request a reduction through a written explanation; maintain all underlying ownership records for inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Registered Office, Corporate Governance, and First Board Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner of the SCSp; optional qualified domiciliation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is physically established or a legally compliant domiciliation agreement is executed with an approved Luxembourg domiciliation service. Hold the first meeting of the general partner (or the first board/management meeting) to adopt the pro forma resolutions, approve the appointment of the manager(s), open the bank account, authorize the e-commerce marketplace seller registration, and delegate routine filing obligations. Record minutes and maintain a statutory corporate register including partners, contributions, manager appointments, and ongoing decisions.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or domiciliation agreement
Minutes of the first board/management meeting
Acceptance of office by the manager
List of partners and capital contribution statement
Corporate governance manual (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the domiciliation agreement is found non-compliant, obtain a new approved domiciliation provider and file a change of registered office with the RCS; if the minutes are challenged during bank onboarding, re-issue a restated resolution with proper date and signature.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no physical industrial establishment; for Amazon FBA e-commerce retail, no industrial license is required under Luxembourg law.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating license required for cross-border internet retail under ISIC 4791; standard business registration through the RCS suffices.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Luxembourg Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - e-commerce marketplace retail does not trigger any Luxembourg EIA registration or permit under the Law of 22 May 2008 on environmental impact assessment, provided no warehousing, logistics, or physical processing is located in Luxembourg.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No direct wastewater, VOC, or waste discharge standards apply to a pure FBA online reseller without physical operations; if the taxpayer later establishes a Luxembourg warehouse, compliance with the Luxembourg general environmental provisions (Law of 21 March 2012 on waste, atmospheric emission thresholds under Grand-Ducal Regulations) would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to a purely online FBA reseller with no physical premises or employees in Luxembourg; if a physical warehouse or office is opened, a fire safety certificate from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and the Luxembourg fire brigade (CGDIS) would be required, plus workplace safety registration with ITM.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income taxes; centralized onboarding via MyGuichet.lu and the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity forming or acting through a Luxembourg SCSp must obtain a Luxembourg business/TIN number. For VAT purposes, the foreign entity or the SCSp (acting for the partners) files a registration form with the AEDT, submitting notarized constitutional documents, economic substance evidence, and details of the appointed local VAT representative if not established in the EU. A Luxembourg tax number (matricule) is issued by the ACD following incorporation; VAT number is issued by the AEDT within a standard processing window of 5-15 business days. A local establishment or VAT representative is required where taxable supplies are made in Luxembourg and the trader has no EU fixed establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SCSp is fiscally transparent by default. The SCSp may elect, by joint declaration of all partners, to be taxed as a taxable corporate entity under the 'opting-in' regime, making it subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax and net wealth tax instead of pass-through taxation. This election is binding and requires prior approval/registration with the Luxembourg direct tax administration. Hybrid mismatch elections are available only to the extent compatible with ATAD-consistent Luxembourg domestic rules (Circulaire LIR n° 212)); no US-style check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 for domestic taxable supplies by small enterprises; for cross-border intra-EU distance sales of goods to consumers a simplified registration threshold of EUR 10,000 (including other intra-EU distance sales) applies within the EU-wide OSS threshold regime; above that threshold the foreign seller must register and charge Luxembourg VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not generally mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping for business-to-business transactions. Structured electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G supplies/sectors under e-invoicing public procurement rules. For all other transactions, e-invoicing is permitted subject to authenticity and integrity controls; archived e-invoices must be retained for at least 6 years. No national tax authority API clearance or continuous transaction controls (CTC) model is lawfully enforced as of the current tax compliance period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically shipped outside the EU and services supplied to non-EU business or private customers under B2B/B2C place-of-supply rules qualify for the 0% VAT rate. The seller must prove physical exit from the EU within the required time limits, hold transport documents, and obtain the export customs declaration. Offshore services to non-established persons are outside Luxembourg VAT scope or zero-rated where the supplier is established in Luxembourg and the recipient's jurisdiction is outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice with export delivery terms (Incoterms 2020)
Transport evidence: Bill of Lading, airway waybill or international carrier packing list
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign bank FX credit confirmation proving actual receipt of export proceeds
Proof of buyer identity, EU exit point, and destination-country customs clearance where available
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities require export evidence to be retained for at least 6 years and will claw back zero-rated treatment, interest, and penalties if the required documentation is incomplete, fraudulent, or not produced timely. For fraudulent export zero-rating, fines up to 200% of evaded tax may be imposed under LIR/LTVAT rules, plus criminal liability (prison sentence) for directors/partners, and the SCSp's tax-transparent partners are jointly and severally liable for non-payment of output VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign exchange administration and applies EU free movement of capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full euro-area convertibility. Current-account and capital-account transactions are unrestricted under Articles 63-66 TFEU, with only narrow EU sanctions/security exceptions. Profit remittance is not subject to FX authorisation or quantitative limits. For an SCSp, which is a transparent partnership, distributions follow contractual profit-share definitions; non-resident partners receiving distributions may be subject to partner-level taxation but no blocking exchange-control permit is required. Banks will verify source of funds and underlying commercial substance for all dividend/profit distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg and the euro-area framework impose no statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in EUR or foreign-currency accounts at a Luxembourg or EU bank. However, EU Regulation 2015/847 wire-transfer traceability rules and AML/CFT obligations require complete originator/beneficiary information on every cross-border payment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-High for payment facilitation and multi-currency treasury support, but Low-to-Medium as a standalone primary bank account. Authorised EU e-money institutions and payment institutions, including Airwallex and Stripe, may hold segregated client funds and offer FX/clearing rails under Luxembourg payment-services law (Law of 10 August 2018 on payment services and e-money, as amended) and the CSSF regime. A Luxembourg SCSp engaged in Amazon FBA may use such providers for operational settlement, but core regulatory treasury discipline requires at least one relationship with a fully licensed Luxembourg credit institution to satisfy KYC credibility, capital escrow comfort, and correspondent-banking clearance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Luxembourg banks require physical or high-assurance video identity verification for authorised signatories, the general partner, and direct/indirect beneficial owners. Remote onboarding is possible only where the bank's risk model permits, the structure is documented as low-risk, and all KYC documentary evidence is notarised/apostilled as required. For an SCSp, the general partner and every ultimate beneficial owner holding more than 25% of capital or control should expect an initial compliance interview; physical attendance by the authorised manager is strongly recommended to avoid multi-week approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque SCSp ownership and non-resident partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed SCSp limited partnership agreement; Luxembourg trade register (RCS) excerpt; up-to-date register of beneficial ownership filed with Luxembourg Business Registers; constitutional documents of all corporate partners; passport copies/proof of address of all natural-person beneficial owners; organisational chart showing ultimate ownership; 15%+ ownership beneficial-ownership declaration forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High Amazon FBA revenue velocity with third-party marketplace receipts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Amazon Seller Central agreements; bank statements of the parent or shareholder proving source of capital; projected cash-flow and transaction volumes; supplier contracts, customs/import invoices, logistics contracts, VAT registration and EU VAT returns; annual financial statements or capital-certification letter; payroll/substance documentation of the Luxembourg entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance of the SCSp in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for Luxembourg premises; local general partner details; local director/gérant appointments and CVs; management board policies and meeting minutes; local bank account mandate; e-commerce P&L and operational evidence including Amazon business reports; sub-accounts or commission agreements supporting actual activities in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for capital injection from non-EU jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank references and statements of the remitting entity; signed declaration of source of funds; audited financial statements of investors; tax residence certificates; conveyance or transfer documentation evidencing the underlying commercial transaction; name-clearance and sanctions screening responses supporting the lawful provenance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions are settled via SWIFT MT103 (if delivered from outside EEA) or SEPA Credit Transfer (if delivered from within SEPA). The beneficiary payment instruction must name the Luxembourg SCSp, reserved IBAN, and bank BIC. The payment reference/purpose field should state clearly: 'Capital contribution to [SCSp name], partnership agreement dated [date], partner [name]'. No foreign-exchange approval or licence is required, but the bank must verify the contributor against the KYC/UBO file and may require completion of BCL statistical reporting forms for balance-of-payments purposes. Capital contribution is accepted only after the adoption/resolution and contractual drawdown notice are produced; cash escrow accounts may be used pending seconded capital calls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade disbursements may be made by SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR within SEPA), SWIFT MT103 (cross-border and non-EUR), or documentary letters of credit issued under ICC UCP 600 for stock purchases from third-country suppliers. Funds received from Amazon FBA sales may be swept from Amazon or a payment facilitator into the Luxembourg operational account via SWIFT/SEPA settlement, then redeployed by commercial invoice, supplier LC, or reverse-factoring arrangements. For USD disbursements, clearing is normally routed through correspondent banks in the United States using CHIPS/Fedwire after conversion at Luxembourg bank rates. All payment orders must carry exact legal entity name, full address, IBAN/BIC, purpose reference, and, where applicable, customs/VAT documentation to prevent AML holds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD forward contracts with licensed Luxembourg or EEA credit institutions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies where physical delivery is not available or where the counterparty requires cash-settlement under ISDA/CSSF-compliant terms
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) executed under ISDA agreements and cleared or bilateral as permitted
FX options and simple option strategies (call/put, collars) with bank counterparties
Liquidity-management FX spot transactions through Luxembourg clearing rails

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg transparent-partnership income tax declaration (déclaration annuelle de la société de personnes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg direct tax administration; filed via eTVA or to the competent bureau d'imposition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December accounting year-end, due by 31 December of the following tax year; an extension is available only upon reasoned request made before the deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessments and administrative fines of EUR 75 to EUR 25,000 for late or incomplete filing; delayed flow-through reporting may trigger late-payment interest at 0.6% per month on final assessed amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of Luxembourg municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC) attributable to the SCSp trade activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) acting for the relevant commune as part of the annual corporate tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory deadline as the annual income tax declaration: 31 December of the year following the fiscal year, with extension only by specific tax-office approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file exposes the SCSp and its manager to administrative fines of EUR 75 to EUR 25,000 and enforced tax collection against partnership assets; late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RBE beneficial-owner declaration / annual corporate-secretarial confirmation of the SCSp ownership register (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven filing within one month after any change in beneficial ownership, including a transfer of partnership interests; for unchanged SCSp entities, an internal annual review is recommended by 31 December or before tax filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false RBE data is punishable by administrative fines and criminal sanctions for wilful misdeclaration; persistent default may expose the manager personally and be published by LBR.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A non-regulated SCSp used for e-commerce is not automatically subject to statutory audit because it has no legal personality; mandatory audit is triggered only if the SCSp is a regulated investment fund, prepares consolidated accounts within a group, or voluntarily opts into company-law audit. As a practical benchmark under Luxembourg small-undertaking exemptions, audit exemption is lost upon exceeding two of three criteria: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and 50 average employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan Comptable Normalisé and commercial accounts rules for transparent partnerships); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for voluntary/consolidated or regulated-fund purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg RBE law is event-driven: the SCSp must file any beneficial-ownership change within one month and there is no separate annual statutory UBO renewal form. The corporate secretary nevertheless performs an annual reconciliation of the RBE record, the internal partner register and any partnership interest transfers, so that shareholding movements are captured and reported on time.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book / resolutions of partners and managers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required for a small SCSp; if contracted for financing or investor purposes, a Luxembourg certified audit typically ranges from $4,000 to $15,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined Luxembourg corporate rate (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + aggregate municipal business trade tax; SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and not an entity subject to CIT)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is classified as a pass-through partnership under Luxembourg tax law; no CIT at SCSp level. Corporate partners resident in Luxembourg benefit from the participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; qualifying e-commerce IP may benefit from the IP box 80% exemption; municipal business tax may apply to the SCSp's permanent establishment/trading activity in Luxembourg.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg corporate income tax return – Formulaire 720; filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu (e-filing for resident companies). For the SCSp itself, an informational partnership return (Formulaire 640) is filed by the general partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Formulaire 720: by 31 May of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; non-calendar year-ends within three months of the balance sheet date. Formulaire 640: for fiscal year ending 31 December, deadline is 31 May of the following year; extensions may be granted via e-filing until 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification and tax registration number (RCS, VAT ID, income tax number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Luxembourg tax registration number of the SCSp and, where applicable, the single corporate partner's Luxembourg identification; non-resident partners are identified on Form 640 attachment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result (commercial profit after adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the SCSp, leave blank at entity level; pass-through results are allocated to partners and reported on their own returns or, for non-resident partners, on the relevant Luxembourg assessment file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forward claimed (CIT and municipal business tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only if the filing entity is a Luxembourg corporate partner; for the SCSp itself, no entity-level loss is available. Municipal business tax loss carry-forward is limited to five years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption gross-up and deduction (dividends and capital gains)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reserved for Luxembourg-resident corporate partners holding qualifying participations; non-resident partners claim relief under applicable DTA or EU directive.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits, and advance payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use for tax withheld at source in foreign jurisdictions on Amazon marketplace revenue or FBA-related payments; attach foreign tax credit schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and signature by authorised representative/general partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Signed by the general partner of the SCSp; for non-resident corporate general partner, signature by that entity's authorised director.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties up to EUR 5,000 plus daily surcharges; late payment interest accrues monthly at 0.8% on outstanding balance; failure to file after formal notice triggers re-assessment at forfeited expense and potential criminal prosecution for concealment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax for Luxembourg resident companies; distributions from an SCSp are not dividends and are not subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax at the SCSp level because the SCSp is fiscally transparent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must deliver a valid Luxembourg Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) to the withholding agent before payment; for payments made through an SCSp, the partners themselves must provide their own TRC and a declaration of underlying economic use. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief requires at least 10% shareholding and a two-year holding commitment; the reduced treaty rate is usually 5% for shareholdings of 10-50% and 0% for qualified shareholdings under the local law participation exemption. The withholding agent files a request for exemption or refund with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments to non-residents (statutory rate 0%). The EU Interest and Royalty Directive provides a further zero-rate treatment for associated enterprises resident in other EU member states. No specific treaty rate is required. Payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions may be subject to a 20% withholding surcharge or disallowance of deductibility under anti-abuse rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue threshold for a Master File; a Luxembourg Local File is required when related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 for goods or EUR 500,000 for services, financing, and intangibles. The SCSp must also maintain contemporaneous documentation where Amazon FBA cross-border operations create related-party flows.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the style of the BVI/UAE; however, the general anti-abuse rule, ATAD implementation, and case law on tax residence and treaty abuse require an SCSp to have substantive presence: local registered office, economic activity, partner/Director decision-making in Luxembourg, bank account, and adequate staff. For Amazon FBA business, the SCSp must not be a shell conduit; the commercial risk and inventory purchases must be supported by real contracts, invoices, and management records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully failing to declare Amazon FBA gross sales and realised revenue through the SCSp, concealing marketplace income streams, or maintaining undisclosed foreign bank accounts for FBA collections.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repair assessment for the tax evaded plus a penalty of up to 100% of the understated tax; daily late-payment interest at 0.8% monthly; criminal fine up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years for egregious concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner or the directors of a corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for civil tax restitution; travel bans, freezing orders, and disgorgement of personal assets may be imposed; conviction can lead to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an SCSp with no real commercial substance solely to house Amazon FBA profits, borrowing treaty benefits, or eliminating Luxembourg municipal business tax exposure without genuine business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty and participation exemption under GAAR; recharacterisation of profits at the partner level; administrative penalty of 25% of the adjusted tax; potential requalification of the SCSp as a taxable Luxembourg entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate general partner directors may be held personally liable for responsible corporate management; exposure to damages and restitution; travel restrictions in serious abuse cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Amazon FBA Fund/Amazon Pay, Stripe, or Airwallex receivables to launder proceeds or to disguise beneficial ownership of the SCSp; failure to maintain know-your-customer records and suspicious transaction reporting on large cross-border flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1 million or 10% of annual turnover for regulated financial intermediaries; for criminal money laundering, imprisonment of five to ten years and seizure of the e-commerce business assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner is subject to civil asset forfeiture; directors who operate the payment accounts without AML controls face criminal liability and suspension of driving/travel rights; non-compliance with beneficial ownership registration exposes directors to custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting Amazon FBA procurement prices, intercompany warehouse fees, or online store commissions at artificial margins to shift profit to a zero-tax jurisdiction or low-tax related party; absence of local file documentation for cross-border related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment to an accurate arm's length result plus secondary recharacterisation of deemed dividends; penalty of 50% of the additional tax due when TP documentation is not contemporaneously prepared and submitted within three months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Tax directors and corporate officers of the general partner can be held jointly and severally liable for civil penalties arising from false or misleading TP reporting; persistent non-compliance leads to regulatory disqualification and travel bans.
